data.title: Mercari, Inc. has fully implemented Forter's AI judgment platform.
data.ai_summary: Mercari fully implemented Forter's AI judgment platform to counter fraudulent credit card transactions, with GMO Payment Gateway providing the API. Preliminary verification showed 3D Secure usage decreased, chargebacks fell to about one-tenth, and credit card GMV improved. The companies will continue supporting Mercari's payment security and customer experience.
data.full_text: Forter, a company providing an AI judgment platform for next-generation commerce (headquartered in New York, USA), and GMO Payment Gateway, Inc. (CEO: Kazunari Aihara, hereinafter referred to as GMO-PG), which is part of the GMO Internet Group, announced that Mercari, Inc. (headquartered in Minato-ku, Tokyo, CEO: Shintaro Yamada, hereinafter referred to as Mercari), which operates Japan's largest flea market app "Mercari," has fully introduced Forter's AI judgment platform as a measure against fraudulent credit card transactions. Forter and GMO-PG jointly verified from the initial stage with Mercari, resulting in the introduction of Forter's AI judgment solution. Additionally, GMO-PG provides an API (Application Programming Interface) that standardly implements Forter's fraud detection function in its online comprehensive payment service "PG Multi-Payment Service." 【Background of Introduction】 Mercari has been implementing various fraud measures to create a safe and secure environment for customers, including measures against fraudulent credit card transactions. Until now, they have applied 3D Secure (Note 1) to transactions deemed necessary for authentication based on their own rules and conducted visual checks for transactions deemed necessary for confirmation. However, as fraudulent methods have become more sophisticated, they faced challenges such as the degradation of the payment experience due to the friction of 3D Secure (Note 2), increased human costs for chargebacks (Note 3), and the need to balance "security assurance" with "providing a smooth payment experience for genuine customers," leading to the selection of a new solution for fraudulent payment measures. (Note 1) A mechanism for authenticating the cardholder in online credit card payments. Card companies may require additional authentication based on the information they hold. (Note 2) The hassle or interruption that users experience during the payment process. This includes transitions to authentication screens and entering passwords. (Note 3) A system where, if a cardholder claims they did not consent to a transaction due to fraudulent use of their credit card, the card company cancels the sales of that transaction, and the merchant bears the cost. 【Selection of Forter and Results of Preliminary Verification】 In the preliminary verification conducted prior to full implementation, Forter demonstrated results exceeding the evaluation criteria set by Mercari in the following three areas: ① Reduced the usage rate of 3D Secure and improved credit card GMV (Note 4) Forter returns a judgment with three options at the time of transaction request: "OK (approved) / NG (rejected) / 3D Secure (recommended)." If it is a three-choice option, merchants (Note 5) can avoid applying 3D Secure to low-risk transactions and focus recommendations on transactions that require judgment. Compliance with the mandatory introduction of EMV 3-D Secure (Note 6) is also automated within the same mechanism. In the preliminary verification, the usage rate of 3D Secure decreased without expanding fraud risk, and credit card GMV improved. ② Reduced chargeback amounts to about one-tenth Forter has a global identity network (Note 7). It analyzes approximately 6,000 data attributes in real-time and assesses reliability for each transaction. Fraudulent methods evolve across borders. Therefore, Mercari emphasized the importance of a global data infrastructure that does not rely solely on its own data during the selection process. Although the chargeback occurrence rate was originally below the industry standard, it further improved in the preliminary verification, keeping chargeback amounts to about one-tenth of the previous system. No incidents were observed where genuine transactions were mistakenly hindered for transactions judged as rejected. ③ Reduced costs for visual checks and rule maintenance Forter updates its AI model and responds in real-time to new fraudulent methods occurring globally. Therefore, merchants do not need to maintain rules on their side. Visual checks are also automated, relieving Mercari of the burdensome manual tasks in fraud prevention. (Note 4) Sales from transactions made using credit cards. (Note 5) Businesses that accept payments via credit cards. In this case, it refers to Mercari. (Note 6) Based on guidelines from the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, it refers to the introduction of EMV 3-D Secure (the latest standard of 3D Secure) required for EC merchants as a measure against fraudulent credit card use. (Note 7) A data infrastructure used to cross-sectionally accumulate transaction histories across multiple businesses to assess the identity and reliability of purchasers. 【Introduction through GMO-PG's Integrated API】 In this introduction, GMO-PG utilizes the Forter integrated interface built on the "PG Multi-Payment Service." Since the series of flows from Forter's fraud detection requests, the application of 3D Secure based on judgment results, to payment processing are consolidated in GMO-PG's API, Mercari was able to introduce Forter as an extension of its existing payment integration. This eliminated the need for separate API connection development and infrastructure construction with Forter, leading to reduced development workload and shortened the period from the start of verification to actual operation. 【Comments from Each Company】 ■ Mercari, Inc. Executive Officer VP of Customer Service / Trust and Safety Marketplace Keisuke Tanaka Mercari prioritizes creating an environment where everyone can conduct transactions safely and securely, and providing a smooth customer experience (UX) that minimizes friction during payment. Until now, we have countered increasingly sophisticated fraudsters with our own fraud detection rules and risk-based judgments of 3D Secure, but we faced a dilemma with genuine customers experiencing "cart abandonment." In the preliminary verification conducted in strong partnership with GMO-PG and Forter, we achieved the result of reducing chargebacks to about one-tenth while improving the success rate of payments, thus increasing credit card GMV. We are now completely free from tuning our own fraud detection rules and visual inspection tasks, and we are confident that we have built a solid payment infrastructure for scalable business development in the future. ■ Forter Country Manager for Japan Yosuke Noda We are very pleased that Mercari, a representative of Japan's e-commerce, has adopted Forter as a partner responsible for enhancing security and customer experience in payments. The results shown in this preliminary verification clearly demonstrate that our real-time judgments based on our global network of 2 billion users not only "shut out fraud" but also "remove friction and enhance GMV and sales." We will continue to support Mercari in the "thorough elimination of fraudulent users" and the enhancement of the "core experience (Core CX)" during payments. ■ GMO Payment Gateway, Inc. Executive Officer Ryo Taninaka As a Payment Service Provider (PSP) providing payment infrastructure to Mercari, and as a partner of Forter, we have been jointly promoting this project from the initial stage. Balancing enhanced payment security with a smooth payment experience for purchasers is a challenge faced by many e-commerce businesses. In this project, by combining Forter's real-time judgments with our payment system, we were able to achieve significant reductions in chargebacks while simultaneously improving GMV. We will continue to support Mercari's business growth through our alliance with both companies and contribute to the development of a safe and secure payment environment in Japan's e-commerce market. 【About Mercari】 Mercari, Inc. operates the flea market app "Mercari" in Japan and the US with the mission of "circulating all values and expanding the possibilities of all people," promoting global expansion through cross-border business. By connecting individuals around the world through the power of technology, we aim to create a rich society where resources circulate and individuals can realize what they want to do. Furthermore, we are engaged in new value creation as a group, including the financial business of Merpay, the cryptocurrency-related business of Mercoin, and the sports business through Kashima Antlers. 【About Forter】 Forter provides optimal AI judgments at every critical stage of commerce. Based on a global identity network, our AI instantly assesses reliability from new registrations to payments and returns. It delivers the best experience to good customers. Ahead of peak season, merchants can now identify trusted AI agents and enable secure, headless checkout with a single no-code integration NEW YORK, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Forter, the Trust Intelligence platform for the future of commerce, introduced new capabilities designed to give commerce leaders the visibility, trust and control to securely embrace this rapidly emerging revenue channel. data.title: Forter launches five AI agents for commerce teams
data.ai_summary: Forter has launched five AI agents for commerce teams as part of its Forter Prism product suite, targeting workflows in fraud analytics, chargeback disputes, abuse prevention, payment approvals, and system integration. The agents are designed to automate manual tasks that merchant teams handle across different functions, reducing manual reviews and improving response times. Forter has also opened early access to its Model Context Protocol, enabling its data to be accessed directly inside general AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude, allowing teams to analyze performance trends and investigate transactions without switching between separate systems.

data.full_text:
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

Forter has launched five AI agents and opened early access to its Model Context Protocol, with the new products aimed at commerce teams handling fraud, payments, disputes and system integration. The rollout expands Forter Prism, the company's agent-based product suite, with tools focused on analytics, chargeback disputes, abuse prevention, payment approval rates and integration work. The agents are designed for specific workflows that merchant teams often handle manually. The Analytics Agent is intended to give users information on risk analysis, transactions, decision rationale, business performance and customer profiles. The Dispute Agent is aimed at automating chargeback disputes, while the Abuse Agent is designed to help merchants set policies around returns, promotions and loyalty misuse. The Payments Agent focuses on payment performance and recommendations intended to lift authorisation rates. The Integration Agent is designed to connect Forter with existing systems through an AI coding assistant that can reduce deployment time. Forter is also making early access available to its Model Context Protocol, or MCP. The system allows Forter's data to be used inside AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude, so merchant teams can work with the information inside software they already use. According to Forter, the protocol lets teams analyse performance trends, investigate transactions and produce executive summaries without switching between separate systems. The same corporate permissions and security controls apply when data is used through those AI tools. The launch comes as merchants face pressure to make faster decisions at key points in the customer journey, including account sign-up, payment approval and post-purchase disputes. Fraud checks, payment issues and customer claims often require staff to gather information from several sources, slowing responses and affecting sales or customer experience. Forter said its products are built on a network of more than two billion shoppers and nearly one million merchants. That data network has become central to how the company positions its fraud and commerce decision tools to retailers and online businesses. AWS was among the outside companies quoted in support of the launch. "The merchants winning right now are the ones who can move from signal to action faster than their competitors, and that gap only grows," said Vince Koh, Global Head, AWS Digital Commerce. "Forter's agents ground fraud and revenue decisions in a network of two billion shoppers, giving commerce teams that edge." Forter has framed the launch as part of a wider shift in online commerce, where AI is changing how consumers discover products, interact with sellers and complete transactions. In turn, merchants must process more information in real time when deciding whether to approve orders, investigate activity or respond to disputes. Workflow focus The five agents map to functions that often sit across different teams. Analytics and payments tend to be handled by commercial and operations staff, disputes by finance or risk teams, and abuse prevention by fraud and customer experience teams. Integration work usually falls to technical teams responsible for connecting third-party software to internal systems. By separating the tools in this way, Forter is targeting practical operational tasks rather than offering a single general-purpose assistant. The approach reflects a broader shift in business software towards narrower AI systems built around defined jobs and data sources. Market pressure Payments and fraud vendors have been adding more AI-led products as merchants look for ways to reduce manual reviews, cut fraud losses and improve approval rates on legitimate transactions. Chargebacks and policy abuse have also become more expensive issues for retailers, especially in sectors with high volumes of returns and promotions. For companies already using large language model tools internally, the MCP element may be one of the more notable parts of the announcement. Rather than requiring staff to sign into a separate dashboard to query Forter data, the protocol is intended to bring that information directly into general AI interfaces already used for internal analysis. Eran Vanounou, Chief Technology Officer, Forter, said the aim was to make the company's data and decision tools easier to use in day-to-day work. "We've always built AI solutions for the people behind commerce who work tirelessly to offer the best experience to their consumers," said Eran Vanounou, Chief Technology Officer, Forter. "Intelligence is now accessible in seconds, in context, and with the accuracy our global network has built over 13 years. These AI agents create a competitive advantage for every Forter customer, who can now accelerate time to impact across the entire customer journey."

data.full_text:
Fraud prevention specialist Forter has launched an artificial intelligence copilot called Forter Prism, as the company reports a sharp rise in automated fraud attempts and agent-driven online shopping activity across its network. The company said it has recorded a 2,107% increase in what it terms agentic activity over the past six months. It also reported a 202% rise in automated fraud attempts over the last year among the 400,000 businesses that use its services. Forter positions Prism as a conversational tool that sits inside its existing portal for merchants. The product focuses on faster investigation of transactions, streamlined analysis, and the creation of dashboards that summarise performance trends. The launch comes as retailers prepare for the 2025 peak shopping season. Many brands face rising volumes of AI-driven traffic and shifting fraud tactics alongside pressure to maintain approval rates and customer experience. Rising agent activity Forter uses the term agentic commerce for transactions or traffic that involve software agents or automated tools. These can research prices, place orders or attempt to exploit vulnerabilities at scale. The company said its latest product updates address what it describes as a visibility gap for merchants. Many businesses struggle to see how much of their traffic and transaction volume involves agents and how much of that activity links to fraud. Forter has expanded its Agentic Activity dashboard with new benchmarks. Merchants can compare their AI-related traffic against aggregated patterns drawn from Forter's global network. The benchmarks show how individual businesses sit against peers on measures such as volume, growth rates and fraud exposure. The company has also added more granular views by region and vertical. It said merchants can examine how agentic commerce differs across markets and sectors and can track shifts over time. Inside Forter Prism Forter Prism functions as an in-portal copilot that responds to natural language queries from merchants. Users can ask questions about specific performance indicators, such as approval rates or chargebacks, and the tool returns summarised data. The company said Prism can explain why a particular metric has changed in recent periods. It can also generate dashboards that present operational views of performance, which would otherwise require manual set-up. Prism includes a transaction investigation feature. It surfaces the data points that Forter's systems used when approving or declining an individual transaction. The copilot then summarises the rationale in non-technical language. One customer described the launch as part of a broader drive for efficiency. "Every retailer, merchant, and direct-to-consumer brand is looking to find ways to be more efficient - not just for the sake of cost savings, but truly to keep pace with the speed of evolving consumer behaviour and expectations", said Rachel Levy, Chief Operating Officer, Brooklinen. "Forter has always stood out in how they put the retailers and brands at the heart of their solutions. With Forter Prism, they are delivering yet another major innovation that will support the balance of revenue generation and consumer satisfaction." Benchmarking fraud risk Forter said many merchants do not know whether AI agents are just referring users or actively making purchases on their sites. The company added that some merchants do not know whether agents feature in fraud attempts against their businesses. The new network benchmarks aim to set a baseline for each customer's exposure to AI-driven traffic. Forter said this should make it easier for merchants to decide which areas of their fraud and customer experience strategies need earlier attention. The firm has also updated its public AI dashboard. It now contains more detailed regional and sector breakdowns and uses AI to generate explanations of the patterns it shows. Forter said the combination of Prism, benchmarks and updated dashboards offers a fuller view of the emerging agentic commerce channel. It argued that this channel is now material for both growth and fraud risk as more consumers and businesses adopt AI tools. Eran Vanounou, Chief Technology Officer at Forter, said the pace of change in the market demanded faster decision-making. "With market shifts and threats moving this fast, businesses can't afford to risk missing a critical agentic insight or manually translate complex data into decisions," said Vanounou. "These latest innovations are giving businesses the speed, insight and confidence to navigate peak season with ease."
